# Results — Study 526 (Intangible-Value) on the real EDGAR + yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly cross-sectional
book-to-market sort (top tertile of intangible-adjusted B/M long, bottom tertile short, one
reporting lag + one execution lag), measured against plain B/M and SPY on a large-cap survivor
basket. As-of **2026-06-27**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Book equity (annual, USD) | 21 FY × 40 names | EDGAR `StockholdersEquity` (10-K) |
| R&D expense (annual, USD) | 20 FY × 20 names | EDGAR `ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense` (10-K) |
| SG&A expense (annual, USD) | 20 FY × 30 names | EDGAR `SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense` (10-K) |
| Shares outstanding (annual) | 20 FY × 40 names | EDGAR `CommonStockSharesOutstanding` |
| Monthly total returns | 256 months × 40 names + SPY | yfinance (auto-adjusted) |
| Monthly prices (market-cap) | 257 months × 40 names + SPY | yfinance (auto-adjusted) |
| Period covered | 2005-02 → 2026-05 (256 months, 21.3 yr) | — |
| Combined fingerprint | `1cfa38af3cb0` | — |

**Source.** SEC EDGAR companyfacts (book equity, R&D, SG&A, shares — 10-K full-fiscal-year facts
only) for 40 long-listed US large-caps spanning the intangible spectrum (intangible-heavy software /
semis / pharma / consumer-brand and intangible-light banks / energy / utilities / retail), plus
yfinance monthly total returns and adjusted closes (for the market-cap denominator) for the same 40
names + SPY. **Intangible capital** = perpetual-inventory capitalisation of R&D (5-yr straight-line
amortisation, *knowledge* capital) + 30% of SG&A (3-yr amortisation, *organisation* capital), per
Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou (2013) and Peters-Taylor (2017). The basket is chosen **by sector, not by
return**.

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is *current* large-cap membership projected
back to 2005; names that delisted are absent. The bias is mild here because **both** legs of the
long/short (cheap value names and expensive growth names) are survivors, so the survivorship tilt is
largely common to the two legs and is *not* a clean push on the spread. Opt in with
`load_real(allow_survivorship_bias=True)`. Treat absolute levels as upper bounds.

## The honest test — intangible-adjusted-B/M long-short

Each month, rank the 40 names by intangible-adjusted B/M; long the top tertile (cheap), short the
bottom tertile (expensive), enter the *next* month (one execution lag), hold one month. One-year
reporting lag on all fundamentals. Equal-weight legs.

| Leg (gross, ann.) | CAGR | Sharpe | maxDD | mean/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Long (cheap, adj-B/M) | +14.95% | 0.85 | −44.6% | +15.68% |
| Short (expensive) | +12.95% | 0.86 | −46.8% | +13.47% |
| **Long-short spread** | **+1.47%** | **0.18** | −44.2% | **+2.21%** |
| S&P 500 (SPY) | +11.11% | 0.78 | −50.8% | +11.70% |

| Signal-axis test (HAC t, n=220 months) | mean/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Long − short (adjusted B/M)** | **+2.21%** | **+0.67** |
| Long − SPY | +3.25% | +1.30 |
| Short − SPY | +1.03% | +0.71 |

The intangible-adjusted-B/M long-short earns **+2.21%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+0.67** — far below the
|t| ≥ 2 bar. Average one-way turnover is a low **4.5%/month** (fundamentals move the ranking slowly).

## Placebo — label-shuffle null (400 draws)

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Adjusted-B/M long-short spread | +2.21%/yr |
| Shuffled null (mean / sd) | +0.00% / 2.12 per yr |
| Spread percentile in null | 85.2 |
| **Placebo two-sided p** | **0.305** |

The real spread sits at the 85th percentile of the shuffled null — *not* in the tail (p = 0.305).
The split of this heterogeneous field is not doing anything a random relabelling could not.

## The Lev-Srivastava adjustment contrast (the third axis)

*Does capitalising intangibles actually beat the plain book-to-market sort?*

| Sort | long-short mean/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Plain** B/M | **−0.16%** | **−0.05** |
| **Adjusted** B/M (R&D+SG&A capitalised) | **+2.21%** | +0.67 |
| **Adjusted − Plain (head-to-head spread)** | **+2.38%** | **+2.93** |

Two things at once: (1) *neither* value sort earns a statistically significant absolute premium on
this modern large-cap survivor tape — plain B/M is **dead flat** (−0.16%/yr) and the adjusted sort
is positive but insignificant; yet (2) the **adjustment genuinely moves the value sort** — the
adjusted-minus-plain spread is **+2.38%/yr at HAC t = +2.93**. Capitalising R&D + SG&A re-ranks the
field enough to flip a flat plain-B/M long-short into a (still-insignificant) positive one. So
Lev-Srivastava's *mechanical* claim — the adjustment changes the value sort and improves it — is
**confirmed on the spread between the two methods**, even though it is not enough to manufacture a
tradable premium out of value investing on this basket.

## Robustness — long/short fraction (adjusted B/M)

| Split | LS mean/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| Halves (0.50) | +0.81% | +0.33 |
| Tertiles (0.33) | +2.21% | +0.67 |
| Quartiles (0.25) | +0.65% | +0.18 |
| Quintiles (0.20) | +4.29% | +1.11 |

No split clears |t| ≥ 2; the spread is small and not robust to the cut.

## Costs + short-borrow

| | mean/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| Long-short **gross** | +2.21% | +0.67 |
| Long-short **net** (10 bps turnover + 100 bps/yr borrow on short) | **+1.20%** | **+0.37** |

Turnover is low (4.5%/month), so costs are not the killer — the signal was never significant gross.
Net of costs the spread is +1.2%/yr at *t* = 0.37.

## Synthetic positive control (faithful-engine check only — not evidence for the tape)

A deterministic monthly panel with a planted annual value premium `edge`. Seed-averaged over 20
seeds (Welch-style robustness for the synthetic claim):

| edge | long-short mean/yr (seed 526) | HAC t (seed 526) | mean HAC t over 20 seeds |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −1.19% | −0.49 | **+0.00** (min −0.32, max +0.43) |
| 0.06 (planted) | +4.81% | +1.97 | — |
| 0.10 (planted) | — | — | **+4.23** (min +3.58, max +4.91) |

At `edge = 0` the harness manufactures **no** significance (mean *t* = 0.00 across seeds); at a large
planted premium it lights up reliably (mean *t* = +4.23, always > 3.5). The engine is faithful, so
the flat real-tape verdict reflects **the market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The intangible-adjusted-B/M long-short earns **+2.21%/yr at HAC t = +0.67**
  (n = 220 months), fails the label-shuffle placebo (percentile 85.2, p = 0.305), and is not robust
  across split fractions. It is **not** statistically distinguishable from zero. WEAK rather than
  NONE only because the underlying value premium and the intangibles-adjustment have strong academic
  support (Fama-French; Lev-Srivastava; Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou) — on broad, non-survivor universes
  the literature documents a real value premium that this 40-name large-cap survivor basket cannot
  reproduce.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 10 bps turnover and 100 bps/yr borrow the spread is **+1.20%/yr
  at t = 0.37**, Sharpe 0.18, max drawdown −44%. There is no tradable edge here; the long and short
  legs are both ~13–16%/yr (they are the same survivor large-caps), and the spread is noise.
- **Does the intangible adjustment beat plain B/M? — CONFIRMED.** Plain B/M is dead flat
  (−0.16%/yr, t = −0.05); the adjustment re-ranks the field and the **adjusted-minus-plain spread is
  +2.38%/yr at HAC t = +2.93**. Lev-Srivastava's mechanical thesis — capitalising R&D + SG&A changes
  and improves the value sort — is confirmed *as a relative statement*, even though it is not enough
  to make value investing print money on this basket.
- **Survivorship — Named.** Current-membership basket projected back to 2005; absolute levels are
  upper bounds, but the bias is largely common to both legs of the long/short.
